conventions.decision: AI full-text eligibility recommendation, distinct from final human/formal inclusion.
conventions.read_extent: Eligibility requires sufficient full-text evidence for every criterion, not independent verification of every proof, appendix or codebase. Inspected extent and version are specified per record.
conventions.features: Only feature_codes fields are verified in this checkpoint. Other legacy feature codes remain provisional. No means not demonstrated in the inspected evidence/version; Partial requires the stated limitation.
conventions.uq: Image UQ includes deterministic sets and posterior variability; it does not imply calibrated probabilities. Operator UQ requires uncertainty for operator parameters, not image variance caused by uncertain physics.
conventions.access: Full texts inspected online. No downloaded paper copies are added to the repository.

records.title: Deep Probabilistic Imaging: Uncertainty Quantification and Multi-modal Solution Characterization for Computational Imaging
records.read_extent: Method, selected toy examples and interferometric case study through real EHT results; Eqs. 9–10, 12–17 and Figs. 4, 6–8. MRI case study and supplements not assessed.
records.technical: A measurement-specific flow approximates the image posterior. Analytic toy comparisons assess posterior accuracy; empirical likelihoods and heuristic diversity weights need not reproduce physical probabilities. Closure observables remove station gains/phases, rather than infer their posterior. Real EHT imaging lacks a reference image. No empirical interval-coverage test is established by these sections.
records.feature_locator: Method, Eqs. 9–10; interferometric case study, Figs. 6–8
records.applicability: Separate analytic posterior approximation tests from acquisition-shift calibration.

3.evidence: Image posterior uncertainty and approximate likelihoods; Method.

4.evidence: Flow method, analytic comparisons and EHT observations.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

quality_followups: Inspect the MRI case study before making modality-wide claims.

records.title: Real-ESRGAN: Training Real-World Blind Super-Resolution With Pure Synthetic Data
records.version: arXiv report 2107.10833, v2; final ICCV Workshops 2021 text not compared
records.read_extent: Main §§3–5, including high-order degradation and §4.4 limitations; training subsection partially inspected; appendix not assessed.
records.technical: Repeated blur, resizing, noise and JPEG plus sinc filtering train a GAN restoration network without explicit operator inference. Real-image examples are qualitative. The limitations describe artifacts and unseen complex degradations; those examples are not calibrated hallucination detection. Compound synthetic training and visually plausible real restoration are already established comparators.

1.evidence: arXiv report 2107.10833, v2; final ICCV Workshops 2021 text not compared

3.evidence: High-order compound degradation and real generalization; §§3–4.

4.evidence: GAN method, ablations, real examples and limitations.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

records.title: Image-to-Image Regression with Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification and Applications in Imaging
records.read_extent: §1.1, §2 including Definition 2.1, Remark 2.2, Algorithms 1–2 and Proposition 2.3; §3.1 and selected §§3.2–3.4. Appendix not audited.
records.technical: RCPS controls expected pixel miscoverage with high probability over iid calibration data, under a shared calibration/test distribution. This is not conditional coverage for every fixed pixel or image. Size-stratified risk is explicitly evaluated. Cell imaging uses a DPC reconstruction as reference; MRI is retrospectively undersampled. Qualitative hallucination examples accompany uncertainty sets.
records.applicability: Stratified uncertainty evaluation itself is not a new contribution.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

quality_followups: Check subject/volume independence before reusing MRI split assumptions.

records.title: Parallel Diffusion Models of Operator and Image for Blind Inverse Problems
records.version: arXiv v1, November 2022; final CVPR 2023 text not compared
records.technical: BlindDPS couples stochastic image and operator processes using learned priors and physical kernel constraints. Experiments use synthetic blur or turbulence within specified functional forms. Section 5 explicitly leaves unknown functional forms unresolved. Joint posterior sampling is present; empirical image/operator coverage and a rejection rule are not established in the inspected experiments.
records.applicability: Joint image/operator sampling already exists; compare model-family assumptions.

1.evidence: arXiv v1, November 2022; final CVPR 2023 text not compared

3.evidence: Unknown operator parameters and joint inference; §3.

4.evidence: Coupled diffusion method and synthetic imaging evaluation; §§3–4.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

records.title: GibbsDDRM: A Partially Collapsed Gibbs Sampler for Solving Blind Inverse Problems with Denoising Diffusion Restoration
records.read_extent: §2, §§3.1–3.3 and §4.1; appendix proofs and audio results not assessed.
records.technical: Partially collapsed Gibbs sampling alternates image restoration with Langevin operator updates. Gaussian measurement noise is specified. Proposition 3.1 requires exact conditional distributions for its stationary-posterior statement; implementation uses approximations. Synthetic FFHQ/AFHQ blur experiments report reconstruction metrics and kernel examples, not calibrated posterior coverage.
records.applicability: Separate sampler target, approximation quality and empirical calibration.

4.evidence: Gibbs method and synthetic deblurring experiments; §§3–4.1.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

quality_followups: Audit conditional approximations before invoking an exact-posterior guarantee.

records.title: Fast Diffusion EM: A Diffusion Model for Blind Inverse Problems With Application to Deconvolution
records.version: arXiv v2, 6 November 2023; final WACV 2024 text not compared
records.technical: An image-sampling E-step alternates with a MAP kernel M-step: the operator is a point estimate shared across image samples. Noise level is supplied. Tests include synthetic blur/noise and an FFHQ prior applied to DIV2K. Figure 4 isolates kernel regularization with a known sharp image, not an end-to-end blind input.
records.applicability: Distinguish content transfer from unseen operator-family robustness.

1.evidence: arXiv v2, 6 November 2023; final WACV 2024 text not compared

4.evidence: Diffusion EM, synthetic tests and component ablations.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

records.title: Blind Image Restoration via Fast Diffusion Inversion
records.read_extent: §§3.1–3.2.3, Algorithms 1–2, selected §4.1, §§4.2–4.5 and §5; appendix not assessed.
records.technical: BIRD optimizes the initial DDIM noise and operator parameters through a deterministic generator. Random initialization alone is not posterior uncertainty. The objective threshold is an optimization stopping criterion, not abstention. Known functional form is required; unknown-form restoration is left open. Experiments include synthetic restoration and combined noise.
records.applicability: Point-estimation comparator with a generative prior.

4.evidence: Inversion algorithm, restoration tests and ablations; §§3–4.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

records.title: Blind Inversion Using Latent Diffusion Priors
records.version: arXiv v1, July 2024; final IEEE TIP 2026 text not compared
records.read_extent: Selected §3, §§4.1–4.2 and application descriptions, §5.1; complete 3D evaluation and appendix not assessed.
records.technical: LatentDEM samples image latents while fitting a MAP operator. Annealed consistency reduces reliance on a poor early operator estimate; it is not an operator posterior. The inspected 2D tests use synthetic motion blur on ImageNet/FFHQ. Joint camera estimation is described, but the full 3D evaluation was not assessed here.
records.applicability: Adaptive consistency weighting already has a direct comparator.

1.evidence: arXiv v1, July 2024; final IEEE TIP 2026 text not compared

3.evidence: Latent image sampling and operator estimation; §4.

4.evidence: Latent EM method and 2D deblurring evaluation.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

quality_followups: Reconcile the inspected preprint with the final journal version before definitive synthesis.

records.title: Uncertainty Quantification in HSI Reconstruction using Physics-Aware Diffusion Priors and Optics-Encoded Measurements
records.read_extent: Main §§3–5 including Tables 1–2 and §4.1 limitations; supplement not fully assessed.
records.technical: HSDiff samples images conditional on specified optics/noise parameters and uses metamer augmentation. Cross-dataset tests evaluate interval coverage and error–uncertainty correlation under several simulated operators. Coverage varies materially by dataset; evaluation is not proof of uniformly calibrated probabilities. Changing a known encoder is distinct from inferring an uncertain operator. Main-text experiments synthesize measurements.
records.applicability: Use ambiguity-sensitive coverage as an existing comparator.

3.evidence: Image uncertainty, metamer ambiguity and domain shift; §§3–4.

4.evidence: Diffusion method, cross-dataset tests and coverage metrics.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

quality_followups: Check supplementary hardware evidence before extending the real-data code beyond inspected main-text tests.

records.title: Blind Inverse Problem Solving Made Easy by Text-to-Image Latent Diffusion
records.version: arXiv report 2412.00557, v1; final workshop text not compared
records.read_extent: Main §§1–5 including Algorithms 1–2, Tables 2–4 and §4.5 examples; appendix not assessed.
records.technical: LADiBI alternates diffusion image updates and optimized operator parameters, not an operator posterior. Synthetic blind JPEG uses a learned U-Net operator; the negative prompt names JPEG artifacts, so analytic-codec independence is not absence of task information. Padding-matched GibbsDDRM changes comparisons. Painting examples are qualitative content transfer; operator fitting occurs per measurement.
records.applicability: Blind nonlinear codec restoration already has a direct comparator.

records.title: ADOBI: Adaptive Diffusion Bridge For Blind Inverse Problems with Application to MRI Reconstruction
records.version: arXiv report 2411.16535, v1; final IEEE TCI 2026 text not compared
records.read_extent: §§2–5 including Algorithms 1–2, Eq. 16, §4.3 and §5.2; appendix not assessed. Missing HTML table entries not transcribed.
records.technical: ADOBI fits coil sensitivity maps around an ESPIRiT initialization while holding sampling/Fourier structure known. Image sampling produces uncertainty maps; operator updates are point estimates. Forward-model calibration means parameter fitting. Error–variance correspondence is shown, but interval calibration is not established. fastMRI measurements are retrospectively undersampled with an additional simulated-noise setting.
records.applicability: Distinguish physical parameter calibration from uncertainty calibration.

records.title: Resolving Blind Inverse Problems under Dynamic Range Compression via Structured Forward Operator Modeling
records.version: arXiv v1, March 2026; final conference text not compared
records.read_extent: §§2.2–5 including Assumptions 3.1/3.3, Algorithm 1, §5.3 and conclusion; proofs not independently audited.
records.technical: CaMB-Diff restricts its estimated operator to stationary, monotone pointwise intensity mappings. Real low-light tests accompany simulated MRI and clipped/noisy HDR. Operator validation uses ground truth as an oracle diagnostic. Plausible clipped-region detail is explicitly generated; physical consistency is not a recoverability certificate. No calibrated image/operator uncertainty is established by these experiments.
records.applicability: Test violations of the stated intensity-mapping family explicitly.

1.evidence: arXiv v1, March 2026; final conference text not compared

2.evidence: Low-light, MRI enhancement and HDR reconstruction; §5.

4.evidence: Structured operator method and multi-task experiments.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

quality_followups: An approximation theorem is not an identifiability or arbitrary-mismatch guarantee.
